NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement

questions.question: Which failure in the identification, authentication, authorization and accounting chain is the PRIMARY cause of the inability to attribute?

options.A: Authentication - the account was protected by a single weak password
options.B: Identification - five people operated the console under one user identity
options.C: Authorization - the account held far more rights than technicians needed
options.D: Accountability - the console failed to log administrative sessions

questions.explanation: Attribution collapsed because the log could name only an identity, and that identity was shared: with five people behind one account, even perfect logging cannot say who acted. (A) is a real weakness - 'Welcome123!' with no MFA made compromise easy - but even a strong, MFA-protected shared account would still leave five suspects; it explains ease of entry, not loss of attribution. (C) is also true of this environment, but excessive rights widened what the insider could do; that goes to impact and does nothing to name him. (D) misreads the evidence: sessions were logged - the record said 'SuperAdmin logged in' - so accountability failed downstream of shared identification; the logging itself worked. Accountability can only ever be as granular as identification; unique identities are the foundation the other IAAA elements stand on.
questions.recallLine: Five technicians share one administrative console account, and no withdrawal can be tied to a person. Which IAAA element's failure is the PRIMARY cause?

optionsShort.A: Authentication: one weak password protected it
optionsShort.B: Identification: five people, one user identity
optionsShort.C: Authorization: rights far exceeded technician need
optionsShort.D: Accountability: console failed to log sessions

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Which link in the chain explains how easily the console admitted an unrostered home computer on one shared secret?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which IAAA weakness decides how much damage a technician can do once the console accepts the shared login?

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Which IAAA element could not do its job once the log could name only 'SuperAdmin' as the actor?

questions.question: Which attack technique is MOST likely to still succeed against the upgraded webmail login?

options.A: Credential stuffing that replays username and password pairs harvested from breaches of unrelated services
options.B: Offline cracking of stolen password hashes using precomputed tables
options.C: A scripted brute-force loop guessing all possible six-digit codes against the login endpoint
options.D: A proxy page that captures and instantly relays both the password and current code

questions.explanation: A TOTP code is bound to a clock, not to the site the user types it into, so an adversary-in-the-middle page can capture the password and the current code and replay both to the real service inside the validity window - the newly deployed control does not break that flow. (A) now fails because a stolen password alone no longer completes login; stuffing would be the residual threat had MFA been skipped. (B) yields passwords and then hits the same second-factor wall; it would be the concern if the question were about theft of an unsalted credential database. (C) is defeated by the 30-second code lifetime combined with ordinary attempt throttling; it would matter only on an endpoint with no rate limiting at all. OTP-based MFA raises the bar yet stays phishable in real time; closing the gap takes an origin-bound, phishing-resistant method such as FIDO2/WebAuthn.
questions.recallLine: Webmail now requires an app-generated time-based code after employees were phished. Which attack technique is MOST likely to still succeed?

optionsShort.A: Credential stuffing with pairs from other breaches
optionsShort.B: Offline hash cracking with precomputed tables
optionsShort.C: Brute-forcing every six-digit code
optionsShort.D: Proxy page relaying password and live code

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Which attack would still work against this webmail had the company deployed no second factor at all?

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Which attack should worry the company if its unsalted password database were stolen?

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Which attack becomes viable against one-time codes on an endpoint that throttles nothing?

questions.question: Which control would MOST reliably have surfaced that accumulation of entitlements earlier?

options.A: SIEM alerting tuned to anomalous use of the finance applications
options.B: Periodic recertification of each user's entitlements by their manager
options.C: A stronger multi-factor policy on all finance system logins
options.D: Automated birthright provisioning for employees joining the firm

questions.explanation: Privilege creep is a state problem, not a behavior problem: the excess rights exist whether or not they are used, so the control that finds them must periodically compare what a person holds against what their current role needs - which is precisely what manager-driven access recertification does, and why it catches transfer-related accumulation. (A) watches usage; it can flag the day the toxic combination is exercised, but dormant excess rights generate no events to alert on - the choice for detecting active misuse. (C) makes it more certain the right person is behind the login without asking whether the login should hold those rights at all. (D) governs the joiner moment; this risk was created by moves, the lifecycle phase birthright provisioning never revisits. Reviews audit entitlement state and monitoring audits behavior; creep hides in the first, so schedule recertification around transfers.
questions.recallLine: An employee who transferred three times can approve invoices, edit vendor records and view payroll. Which control would MOST reliably surface that accumulation earlier?

optionsShort.A: SIEM alerts on anomalous finance-application use
optionsShort.B: Managers periodically recertify each user's entitlements
optionsShort.C: Stronger MFA on finance system logins
optionsShort.D: Automated birthright provisioning for new joiners

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Which control tells the company the day a toxic combination of finance rights is actually exercised?

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Which control makes it certain the person logging into the finance system is who the account claims?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Which control gives a new joiner the correct starting access on their first day in a role?

questions.question: Which figure gives the fairest single basis for comparing the three products?

options.A: The lowest false acceptance rate that each vendor quotes in its datasheet
options.B: The false rejection rate each vendor measured during its own pilot
options.C: The failure-to-enroll rate observed across the user population
options.D: The crossover error rate, where false accepts and false rejects are equal

questions.explanation: Since FAR and FRR both move with the threshold, any vendor can make either number look excellent by choosing where to measure; the crossover point removes that freedom by fixing the comparison at the setting where the two error rates meet, so a lower CER genuinely means a more accurate sensor. (A) and (B) are each one end of a tunable trade - quoting either alone is exactly the marketing trick the analyst has run into, though each becomes relevant again when tuning the chosen product for its site's risk bias. (C) measures how many users can register at all, which matters for usability and population coverage but says nothing about matching accuracy once enrolled.
questions.recallLine: Three fingerprint vendors quote error rates measured at thresholds each chose. Which figure gives the fairest single basis for comparing the products?

optionsShort.A: Lowest false acceptance rate each vendor quotes
optionsShort.B: False rejection rate from each vendor's pilot
optionsShort.C: Failure-to-enroll rate across the user population
optionsShort.D: Crossover error rate, where both rates meet

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Which figure matters once a sensor is chosen and is being tuned to admit fewer impostors at a high-risk door?

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Which number tells the bank how often its own staff will be turned away by the sensor it picked?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which figure tells the bank how many staff will not be able to register fingerprints at all?

questions.question: Now that one login unlocks everything, which recommendation about protecting the portal credential is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Rotate the retired downstream application passwords on a shorter schedule
options.B: Keep separate standalone passwords for the three most sensitive applications
options.C: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication at the portal login
options.D: Extend the portal session lifetime so users authenticate less often

questions.explanation: Single sign-on deliberately concentrates authentication risk: convenience rises, and the portal credential becomes the key to the kingdom, so the proportionate response is to harden that one credential to a level none of the forty passwords ever needed - strong MFA resistant to real-time phishing. (A) polishes credentials that SSO has made largely irrelevant to the attack path; rotation there would matter if legacy direct logins remained exposed. (B) quietly abandons SSO for the crown jewels, an admission of defeat that also multiplies user friction - defensible only where a system genuinely cannot integrate. (D) moves in the wrong direction, lengthening the window a hijacked session stays valid.
questions.recallLine: Forty applications now sit behind one sign-on portal. Which recommendation about protecting the portal credential is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: Rotate retired downstream application passwords faster
optionsShort.B: Keep standalone passwords for three sensitive applications
optionsShort.C: Require phishing-resistant multi-factor at the portal
optionsShort.D: Extend session lifetime so users authenticate less

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Which housekeeping still matters if some applications kept direct logins that bypass the new portal?

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: What should the bank do about an application that genuinely cannot be integrated behind single sign-on?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Which change cuts how often staff are asked to re-authenticate during a working day?

questions.question: Which process change MOST directly ends a departing employee's access before the termination window opens?

options.A: Trigger automatic account suspension from HR termination workflow events
options.B: Add a quarterly manager recertification of every technician's access
options.C: Shorten the maximum password age on privileged accounts to thirty days
options.D: Collect badges, tokens and master keys during each exit interview

questions.explanation: The gap is timing: the organization knew termination was coming before the employee did, and only an automated feed from the HR workflow converts that knowledge into disabled access at the right moment, uniformly across every site. (B) is the correct tool for finding quietly accumulated rights, but a quarterly cadence can trail a termination by months - wrong cadence for an event-driven risk. (C) rotates a credential the departing insider still legitimately holds until the rotation lands; it narrows a different exposure, stale secrets. (D) matters and should continue, but it recovers physical credentials at or after the exit conversation - hours or days inside the very window the lead wants closed, and it touches nothing logical. Deprovisioning is an event, not a review; wire identity systems to HR triggers so access dies the moment trust does.
questions.recallLine: The bank knows a technician is being terminated before he does. Which process change MOST directly ends his access in that window?

optionsShort.A: Automatic suspension from HR termination workflow events
optionsShort.B: Quarterly manager recertification of technician access
optionsShort.C: Thirty-day maximum password age on privileged accounts
optionsShort.D: Collect badges and tokens at exit interview

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Which review would eventually reveal that a departed technician's account is still enabled months later?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which policy narrows the exposure from privileged credentials that sit unchanged for years at a time?

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Which step recovers the badge, token and master keys a leaver still physically holds?

questions.question: Which password storage design BEST resists offline cracking the next time a table is stolen?

options.A: Unsalted SHA-512 digests, substituting a longer modern hash for MD5
options.B: Per-user salts fed into a slow, memory-hard function such as Argon2
options.C: AES-encrypted passwords with the key kept in the application's config file
options.D: Salted MD5 digests, retaining the fast algorithm but defeating rainbow tables

questions.explanation: Offline cracking is an economics problem, and this design attacks both terms: unique salts force the attacker to work per-user with no precomputed tables, while a deliberately slow, memory-hard function cuts guessing from billions per second to thousands - the approach NIST SP 800-63B prescribes for memorized secrets. (A) swaps one fast, unsalted digest for another; SHA-512's extra bits do nothing against lookup tables or GPU throughput. (C) makes passwords recoverable by design, and an attacker who stole the database from the application environment plausibly has the config file key too - encryption belongs at other layers, not as the password store. (D) is half the fix: the salt kills precomputation, but MD5's speed still permits enormous per-user guessing rates against weak passwords.
questions.recallLine: Brackley must redesign password storage so the next stolen table resists offline cracking. Which storage design BEST achieves that?

optionsShort.A: Unsalted SHA-512, a longer modern digest
optionsShort.B: Per-user salts into a slow memory-hard function
optionsShort.C: AES encryption, key in the application config
optionsShort.D: Salted MD5, fast but rainbow-table proof

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Which change answers an auditor who objects to MD5 only because the algorithm is old and its digest short?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which protection suits data the application must be able to read back again, such as stored account numbers?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Which single change stops attackers reusing a rainbow table computed years ago against the stolen digests?

questions.question: A scheduling app must read users' calendars at a third-party provider without ever seeing their passwords. Which framework should the team implement?

options.A: OAuth 2.0, so each user authorizes a scoped access token for the app
options.B: OpenID Connect, so the app receives a signed ID token identifying each authenticated user
options.C: SAML 2.0, so the provider asserts each user's authentication to the app
options.D: Kerberos delegation, so the app forwards each user's service tickets

questions.explanation: The requirement is delegated authorization - let this app read my calendar, nothing more, no password shared - and that is OAuth 2.0's exact purpose: the user consents at the provider, and the app receives an access token limited to the calendar scope. (B) tells the app who the user is, and identity alone confers no right to read resource data; OIDC would be the pick if the app merely needed login. (C) likewise asserts authentication between organizations and carries no resource-scoped delegation for an API. (D) is an intra-domain mechanism for services acting on behalf of users inside one Kerberos realm, not a consumer-web pattern across providers. OAuth answers what may this app touch; OIDC and SAML answer who is this user.
questions.recallLine: A scheduling app must read users' calendars at a third-party provider without ever seeing their passwords. Which framework should the team implement?

optionsShort.A: OAuth 2.0: user authorizes a scoped token
optionsShort.B: OpenID Connect: signed ID token naming the user
optionsShort.C: SAML 2.0: provider asserts the user's authentication
optionsShort.D: Kerberos delegation: app forwards the user's tickets

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Which standard should the team pick if the app only needed to know which user had signed in?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which standard lets employees open the partner-hosted benefits portal with their corporate directory login?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Which mechanism lets a service act for a user against other servers inside one Windows domain?

questions.question: Which cause should the engineer investigate FIRST for the rejected codes?

options.A: Clock drift on the migrated server breaking time-step agreement
options.B: Counter desynchronization between the apps and the server
options.C: Corrupted shared seeds requiring re-enrollment of every authenticator
options.D: An expired TLS certificate on the affected validation endpoint

questions.explanation: TOTP validation computes a code from the shared seed and the current 30-second time step, so both sides must agree on the time - and virtual machine migrations are a classic way for one guest's clock to drift while its peer stays true, which matches the evidence exactly: same users, same seeds, one server rejecting. (B) describes HOTP, the counter-based variant; authenticator apps here are time-based, and a counter problem would follow the user, not the server. (C) cannot explain codes validating on the peer, since both servers verify against the same seeds - seed corruption would fail everywhere. (D) would stop clients connecting or produce certificate errors, not clean rejections of otherwise well-formed codes. When one validator rejects what another accepts, suspect whatever differs between them; for TOTP that is almost always the clock.
questions.recallLine: After a hypervisor migration, one authentication server rejects every authenticator code its peer accepts. Which cause should the engineer investigate FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Clock drift breaking time-step agreement
optionsShort.B: Counter desynchronization between apps and server
optionsShort.C: Corrupted seeds requiring re-enrollment of every authenticator
optionsShort.D: Expired TLS certificate on the validation endpoint

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Which fault explains rejected codes when the tokens are counter-based and one user's button presses outran the server?

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Which cause would explain codes from every authenticator being rejected by both servers at once?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Which fault would leave clients unable to reach the validation endpoint at all after the migration?

questions.question: Which access control model fits the requirement that no file owner may override or reclassify?

options.A: Role-based access control driven by job assignments
options.B: Discretionary access control administered by resource owners
options.C: Mandatory access control enforced through security labels
options.D: Attribute-based access control evaluating contextual rules

questions.explanation: Two phrases in the stem are decisive: classification markings, and decisions imposed by the system beyond any owner's authority - the defining pair of properties of mandatory access control, where subjects hold clearances, objects hold labels, and policy is centrally enforced. (A) grants by job function and would let an administrator or role owner adjust assignments, which the requirement excludes; it fits an enterprise organizing access around positions. (B) is the direct opposite of the requirement, since discretion by the owner is exactly what must be removed. (D) could emulate labels among its attributes, but its purpose is dynamic, condition-based decisions rather than a rigid lattice of clearances - the right answer when access must vary with time, location or device.
questions.recallLine: A document system must enforce government classification markings so that no file owner can reclassify. Which access control model fits that requirement?

optionsShort.A: Role-based, driven by job assignments
optionsShort.B: Discretionary, administered by resource owners
optionsShort.C: Mandatory, enforced through security labels
optionsShort.D: Attribute-based, evaluating contextual rules

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Which model suits an enterprise that wants access to follow the positions people hold?

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Which model leaves each document's creator free to decide who may read it?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Which model suits decisions that must vary with the time, location or device of each request?

questions.question: Which characteristic of the file share environment made the company-wide readability possible?

options.A: Rule-based control applies one uniform policy to every subject
options.B: Discretionary control leaves grant decisions with each resource owner
options.C: Mandatory control ties every access decision to clearance levels
options.D: Role-based control links permissions to defined job functions

questions.explanation: Windows NTFS permissions follow the discretionary model: whoever owns a file may share it at will, so a well-meaning creator can quietly grant the world access to regulated data, and that owner discretion is the exact mechanism the auditor observed. Option (A) describes system-wide rules such as firewall-style conditions; had one uniform policy governed the share, individual creators could not have loosened it, and the finding would look different. (C) would have made the oversharing impossible, since labels and clearances remove the owner's choice; it explains a different environment, not this one. (D) would bound access by job function, and the finding shows access following individual grant decisions, not roles. DAC's convenience is its risk: owner-controlled sharing scales into uncontrolled sprawl unless monitored or replaced for sensitive data.
questions.recallLine: Cardholder spreadsheets on a Windows share were readable company-wide. Which characteristic of that file share environment made that possible?

optionsShort.A: Rule-based: one uniform policy for every subject
optionsShort.B: Discretionary: owners decide their own grants
optionsShort.C: Mandatory: decisions tied to clearance levels
optionsShort.D: Role-based: permissions linked to job functions

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Which model applies a single system-wide condition to every subject, whoever created the file?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which model would have prevented the oversharing outright by removing the creator's discretion?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Which model would have bounded access to those spreadsheets by the job each employee holds?

questions.question: Which replacement practice would BEST bring physical key handling into line with identity principles?

options.A: Issue keys individually from an audited cabinet with per-person sign-out records
options.B: Install a camera covering the key storage area so removals can be reviewed
options.C: Move the keys into a locked cabinet whose combination all technicians share
options.D: Remove the identifying label so the keys' purpose is hidden from a visitor

questions.explanation: Physical keys are credentials, and the case study's core lesson - one identity per person, with attributable use - applies to them exactly as it does to logins. An audited cabinet with individual sign-out restores identification and accountability for every key movement. (B) is purely detective: footage may show who took a key after cash has gone, and cameras are a sound complement once issuance is controlled. (C) upgrades the container but recreates the SuperAdmin defect in physical form - a shared combination is a shared credential, so no removal can be attributed. (D) is security through obscurity; a labeled drawer made the attack easier, but an unlabeled unlocked drawer is still an uncontrolled credential store.
questions.recallLine: Safe master keys sit in an unlocked drawer any office visitor could reach. Which replacement practice BEST aligns key handling with identity principles?

optionsShort.A: Audited cabinet with per-person sign-out records
optionsShort.B: Camera covering the key storage area
optionsShort.C: Locked cabinet with a shared combination
optionsShort.D: Remove the label identifying what keys open

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: How would the firm establish afterwards who removed a master key from the storage area?

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Which change stops a passing visitor reaching into the drawer and lifting a master key?

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Which change keeps a visitor from learning which doors the keys in that drawer open?

questions.question: Which risk does the split-knowledge arrangement MOST directly address?

options.A: A single trusted insider misusing the complete secret alone
options.B: Losing access to the vault when one officer resigns abruptly
options.C: Disclosure of the combination while it is first distributed
options.D: Systematic manipulation of the vault's mechanical dial

questions.explanation: Splitting the secret means no individual ever possesses enough knowledge to act, so exploiting the vault demands collusion between two trusted people - a dramatically rarer event than one insider going bad, as the QuickCash case illustrates. (B) gets the effect backwards: split knowledge worsens availability, since a departed officer takes an irreplaceable half with them; that is a cost of the scheme, managed through escrow or recovery procedures, not a benefit. (C) is untouched - each half must still be conveyed to its officer somehow, and a distribution channel leak remains possible for both halves. (D) concerns the lock's physical attack resistance, which no knowledge-management arrangement changes.
questions.recallLine: Two officers each memorise half a vault combination and neither may learn the other. Which risk does that split-knowledge arrangement MOST directly address?

optionsShort.A: A lone insider misusing the whole secret
optionsShort.B: Losing vault access when an officer resigns
optionsShort.C: Disclosure while the combination is first distributed
optionsShort.D: Manipulation of the vault's mechanical dial

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Which cost does splitting the combination create, and what do escrow and recovery procedures exist to manage?

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Which risk remains at the moment each officer is first told the half entrusted to them?

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Which risk is addressed by the rating of the lock itself rather than by how its secret is held?

questions.question: Which remediation BEST addresses both findings on the service account?

options.A: Rotate the service account password and store it in the team's vault
options.B: Rename the account to obscure its function from observers
options.C: Enroll the service account in the company's standard MFA program
options.D: Scope the account to minimum required rights and block interactive logon

questions.explanation: The review surfaced two distinct defects - excessive privilege and human use of a machine identity - and the remediation must close both: least-privilege scoping removes the domain-admin blast radius, while a deny-interactive-logon policy forces technicians back onto their own accounts, restoring attribution. (A) is sound hygiene that leaves both findings standing; the freshly rotated secret still carries domain admin and technicians can still check it out to log in. (B) is obscurity - an attacker enumerating privileged group membership finds the account whatever it is called. (C) misfits the account type: unattended software cannot answer interactive MFA prompts, so enrollment would break the monitoring service without reducing its privileges.
questions.recallLine: A monitoring service account holds domain administrator rights, and technicians sign in with it interactively. Which remediation BEST addresses both findings?

optionsShort.A: Rotate the password and vault it
optionsShort.B: Rename the account to obscure its function
optionsShort.C: Enroll the service account in standard MFA
optionsShort.D: Scope rights down and block interactive logon

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Which hygiene step should follow, once the account's rights and its human use have been dealt with?

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Which change makes a privileged account slightly harder to spot for someone skimming the user list?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Which control belongs on the technicians' own named accounts, which can answer a prompt?

questions.question: What must happen BEFORE a directory account is issued to a seasonal adjuster?

options.A: A manager's attestation that the applicant is genuine is recorded in the onboarding ticket.
options.B: The license is validated with the issuing authority and matched to the applicant.
options.C: A hardware authenticator is issued and bound to the adjuster at first sign-in.
options.D: An email verification link is sent and clicked to confirm the applicant's address.

questions.explanation: Enrollment has an order, and the order is the control. NIST SP 800-63A resolves, validates and verifies the claimed identity; only then does SP 800-63B bind an authenticator to the subject that proofing produced. Validating the license with the issuing authority and matching the document to the person presenting it is what makes the resulting account refer to a human being. A is an authorization to create the account rather than evidence of who will hold it, and a hiring manager can be socially engineered as easily as a mailbox. C is necessary, but binding a token to an unproven identity yields a well-protected fiction. D demonstrates control of an email address, which is address-of-record confirmation, adequate for a self-service newsletter and not for a claims adjuster who can release payments. Decide what an identity asserts before deciding how hard it is to steal.
questions.recallLine: Before a seasonal adjuster's account is created, which step establishes that the applicant is the person hired?

optionsShort.A: A manager's attestation filed in the ticket
optionsShort.B: Validate the license with the issuing authority
optionsShort.C: Bind a hardware authenticator at first sign-in
optionsShort.D: Click an emailed verification link

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: What keeps a proofed adjuster's stolen password from being enough to sign in?

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: How does a portal confirm it can reach the address a registrant gave?

questions.question: Which mechanism MOST directly enforces the $50,000 condition without depending on who the trader is?

options.A: Grant a role to the traders who are authorized to place large orders.
options.B: Let each desk head decide at their discretion who may exceed the limit.
options.C: Deny orders above the threshold when the request comes from an unmanaged device.
options.D: Label orders and workstations by sensitivity and let the system compare the labels.

questions.explanation: Access control models differ in what the decision is a function of. Role-based decisions are a function of the subject's job, discretionary decisions a function of an owner's choice, and mandatory decisions a function of labels carried by subject and object. A rule-based decision is a function of the request's own attributes, such as amount, device state and network, and it applies identically to the newest trader and the head of the desk, which is what a compliance condition written about orders rather than about people needs. A puts the condition on the person, so a trader holding the role keeps it on an unmanaged laptop at home. B makes the limit negotiable by the manager most motivated to waive it. D would work, and imposes a labeling scheme across every order and workstation to express one threshold. Read the requirement and ask what the decision has to be a function of.
questions.recallLine: A rule applies to every trade over a set amount regardless of the trader. Which access control model MOST directly expresses it?

optionsShort.A: A role for large-order traders
optionsShort.B: Desk heads waive the limit at discretion
optionsShort.C: Deny above-threshold orders from unmanaged devices
optionsShort.D: Compare sensitivity labels on orders and workstations

questions.question: Which step should Kentmere take FIRST on the unowned overnight service account?

options.A: Rotate the key and move it into the platform team's secrets manager.
options.B: Move the scheduled task onto the hardened jump host the platform team maintains.
options.C: Ask the billing manager to approve the account at the quarterly access review.
options.D: Record the account in the service-account register with a named owning team.

questions.explanation: A service credential nobody owns cannot be corrected safely, because every other step on this list needs someone who knows what breaks. Ownership is the entry that gives a credential a lifecycle: a team to right-size its rights, a team to answer at rotation time, a team to decommission it when the meter-data feed is retired. NIST SP 800-53 AC-2 assigns account managers for exactly that reason. A is the second step and a good one, and rotating a key whose consumers are unknown stops the nightly billing run at two in the morning. B changes where the task executes and leaves a full read-write credential sitting in a scheduled job. C asks a manager who does not own the account to certify it, converting an unowned account into an approved unowned account. Give a non-human identity a human name before giving it anything else.

optionsShort.A: Rotate the key into a secrets manager
optionsShort.B: Run the task on a hardened host
optionsShort.C: Manager approves it at quarterly review
optionsShort.D: Register the account with a named owner

domains.title: Security Assessment and Testing
domains.caseStudy:
Domain 6 is how you find out whether controls work: vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, code testing, log review, audits, and the metrics that tell management what the results mean.

Case Study: The "Unchecked Validator" Logic Bomb

### Context

FinCorp rushed a mobile check deposit feature for its ATM app to beat a competitor to market. Three weeks behind schedule, the VP of Engineering waived the security gate review and promised to fix anything found afterwards. The feature let a user type the check amount by hand.

### What went wrong

A researcher entered a negative amount. The balance logic subtracted the deposit as written: balance minus negative one hundred is balance plus one hundred. Money appeared from nothing.

Four things had to fail for that to ship. Functional testing covered the happy path and no edge cases, so nobody typed a minus sign. No static analysis ran, and a SAST tool would have flagged the unvalidated integer. The vulnerability scanner was running, but the new application server's IP range had been dropped from the scan scope during a firewall change. No penetration test was commissioned, and a tester with ten minutes and a sense of what a deposit should never do would have found it.

The ATM industry has its own business-logic flaw, and the white paper documents it under transaction reversal fraud. The criminal times a card-reader fault so the host reverses a withdrawal whose cash has already been staged, then forces the shutter. It works because the host's reversal logic trusts the wrong signal. No scanner finds that; it takes someone who understands the transaction state machine and tests it on purpose. The negative deposit is the same class of defect on the deposit side.

### What a practitioner does differently

The test plan carries negative, boundary and abuse cases, written from the question "what must this feature never do?" Static analysis runs in the build pipeline on every commit. Dynamic testing and a penetration test run against pre-production, with business-logic cases in the scope, not only the OWASP checklist.

Scan scope is tied to the asset inventory through change control, so the firewall change that moved the server also updated the scanner's targets. A gap in scope is a gap in coverage, and the metric that reports "no critical findings" is worthless if it silently excludes the newest system.

The security gate cannot be waived by the person who benefits from waiving it. A waiver is a risk acceptance: it is signed by the risk owner, recorded, time-boxed, and reviewed. And the researcher needs a door: a published disclosure policy so the report lands with security instead of on social media.

### Outcome

The researcher reported the flaw through a support address, and FinCorp closed it. The postmortem replaced "fix it in post" with a gate that only the risk owner can defer, and put the application server back in the scanner's scope.

### What the exam tests

Expect questions distinguishing assessment, audit and testing; SAST versus DAST versus manual review and what each can and cannot find; penetration-test phases and rules of engagement; misuse-case and negative testing; scan scope and coverage as management metrics; and who is allowed to accept a risk.

### Related reading

The firm in this scenario is a composite. The ATM analogue and the controls are documented in:

- [Technical Risks and Attack Vectors Targeting ATMs](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-technical-risks-white-paper.pdf), the sections on transaction reversal fraud and on monitoring, auditing and incident response (audits, vulnerability assessments, penetration tests).
- [ATM Security Capability Maturity Worksheet](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-capability-maturity-worksheet.pdf), Domain 4, process and governance controls.

stimuli.title: FinCorp: the second report
stimuli.text: FinCorp's mobile check deposit accepted a negative amount and credited the customer, and the story reached the press. Nine days later its security mailbox receives a second report. An independent researcher writes that the same mobile deposit endpoint accepts an amount carrying sixteen decimal places, and that the balance service rounds it in the customer's favor. She has not published, gives a ninety-day deadline, and asks for a named contact. FinCorp has no vulnerability disclosure policy, no bug bounty, and no stated position on researchers who test its live application. The VP of Engineering who waived the pre-release security review still owns the release schedule. Legal's first draft reply threatens action under the terms of service.

profile.organization: FinCorp · mobile check deposit for ATM customers
profile.regime: State banking examination · card brand rules
profile.environment: Mobile deposit endpoint · balance service · no disclosure policy
profile.state: Day nine after a related flaw went public, second report in hand

stimuli.title: A deposit of minus one hundred
stimuli.text: FinCorp's mobile check deposit feature passed every functional test before launch: deposits with valid amounts posted correctly on every device. A researcher later added funds to an account by entering a check amount of minus one hundred, which the application accepted. The chief information security officer wants to know why the weekly vulnerability scan, which ran with current plugins against the correct address range, never reported it. The team also wants the missing input-validation check flagged automatically in the build pipeline, before the application is ever deployed to a test server, and wants evidence the board can rank spending against.

profile.environment: Feature passed every functional test · weekly credentialed scan of the estate
profile.state: Researcher added funds by entering a negative amount

stimuli.title: Testing from the outside in
stimuli.text: Kingsmere Insurance is scoping two pieces of assessment work. A security engineer must assess a third-party web application for injection flaws: the vendor will provide no source code and no design documents, but a fully functional staging instance is available. Separately the insurer has commissioned a test of its own customer portal and directed that the testers receive only the public address, with no credentials, diagrams or code, so the result reflects what an uninformed internet attacker could achieve. A security manager must also baseline missing patches across 4,000 servers monthly with two staff.

profile.environment: Third-party application with no source available · 4,000 servers across three data centers
profile.state: Two engagements being scoped

stimuli.title: Scanning what is actually there
stimuli.text: A scan of Kingsmere Insurance's database servers, run without credentials from an adjacent network segment, reports only banner-level findings and misses local misconfigurations the database team knows exist. A post-incident review has separately found that a firewall change had removed a new application server's subnet from the scanner's target list, so for months the reports showed the environment clean while that server sat unassessed. The insurer's test lead wants an automated way to discover how a service handles input its developers never anticipated, without writing a case for each one.

profile.environment: Database servers scanned without credentials from an adjacent segment · scanner target list edited by a firewall change
profile.state: Coverage and depth both questioned

stimuli.title: When the tool and the truth disagree
stimuli.text: A scanner has reported a critical injection flaw in a human resources application at Ravenscar Building Society. The application team demonstrates that the flagged parameter is fully parameterised, and a retest with a manual proof-of-concept confirms the code is safe. Before releasing a new payment module the development manager wants the most thorough security assessment possible, and has budgeted time for reviewers to use full source code, configuration files and architecture diagrams. An assessment of a twenty-year-old machine estate must separately establish whether any units still answer on the maintenance modems the original vendor installed.

profile.environment: Scanner reporting a critical injection flaw · payment module release pending
profile.state: Findings being adjudicated

stimuli.title: Reading the code and reading the logs
stimuli.text: Ravenscar Building Society's development manager has instituted a rule that no change to the deposit service merges until a second developer has read the diff line by line, checking input handling and error paths against the secure-coding standard. A regulator has separately asked the society to categorize its weekly review of application logs within a control framework: the review finds fraud patterns after transactions occur and does nothing to stop one completing. Two days after a critical flaw in a remote-access appliance was published with a detection check, a credentialed scan reported the appliance clean.

profile.environment: Line-by-line review before every merge · weekly log review categorized for a regulator
profile.state: Practices being formalised

stimuli.title: Naming a thing the same way twice
stimuli.text: Analysts at Ravenscar Building Society waste hours arguing whether a bug named in a vendor advisory and a flaw found by the scanner are the same issue, and the manager wants every tool, ticket and advisory to refer to each publicly known vulnerability by one common identifier. A fraud investigation separately depends on an application's audit trail, and counsel warns the records will only stand up if the society can show they remained unaltered after being written, including by the administrators who operate the logging platform. A release manager fears a fix could quietly re-break working validation.

profile.environment: Analysts arguing over whether two reports describe one flaw · audit trail relied on in a fraud case
profile.state: Common identifiers being adopted

stimuli.title: Four thousand findings and one patch team
stimuli.text: Colebrook Payments' latest scan produced 4,000 findings and the patch team can address only a fraction each month, so the manager wants an open, vendor-neutral way to rank them by technical severity as a starting point. The operations center separately receives an alert for every single failed console login and now ignores the queue entirely, while genuine brute-force attempts drown in the noise. Operations also want to know the deposit service is working end to end at three in the morning, before any real customer hits an error.

profile.environment: 4,000 open findings · every failed login alerted individually · overnight service checks wanted
profile.state: Prioritization and noise both unresolved

stimuli.title: Assurance somebody else will accept
stimuli.text: Colebrook Payments is outsourcing transaction processing and wants third-party assurance that the provider's security and availability controls operated effectively across the last twelve months, in a report its own auditors can review in detail. External financial auditors have separately asked about a payroll service provider: specifically whether that provider's processing controls could cause misstatements in Colebrook's financial statements. A researcher's fuzzing campaign keeps dying at the first field because corrupted samples break a checksum, and the team has now obtained the format specification. Real customer experience during an outage needs analysis.

profile.environment: Transaction processing being outsourced · payroll provider in the audit scope
profile.state: Reports being requested from two providers

stimuli.title: Shifting the work earlier
stimuli.text: A post-incident review at Ellesmere Trust found that a defect would have cost minutes to fix at design time, days at code review and millions after launch, and the chief information security officer's recommendation is to shift security work earlier. A junior assessor must separately verify 300 machine images against the hardening standard, confirming services disabled, patches applied and default accounts removed, and produce consistent repeatable evidence for each. Financial auditors want assurance about a payroll provider's effect on the trust's statements, and the certification auditor wants evidence leadership examines results.

profile.environment: Defect cost rising by phase · 300 machine images against a hardening standard
profile.state: Program direction being set

stimuli.title: Testing what the parts do together
stimuli.text: A deposit feature at Ellesmere Trust failed even though the mobile client, the middleware and the core banking system each passed their own test suites: the middleware forwarded an unvalidated amount, assuming the client had checked it. An auditor must separately verify that documented role separation on the machine management console actually holds, that a field-technician login cannot invoke the administrator functions the documentation says are restricted. A researcher has shown that two simultaneous deposits from one account sometimes credit both, because the balance check and the balance update are separate steps. A federal partner needs assessment procedures.

profile.organization: Ellesmere Trust · integration and access testing
profile.environment: Mobile client, middleware and core each passing their own suites · role separation documented but unverified
profile.state: Integration defects reaching production

stimuli.title: Who is allowed to say it is fine
stimuli.text: An internal auditor at Ellesmere Trust must verify that 12,000 user-access reviews completed last year were each signed off by the correct manager, and checking every record would take longer than the audit window allows. External auditors separately need to inspect firewall configurations and server settings over six weeks, and the network team has proposed issuing them the same administrator credentials the engineers use. The trust's own payment-processor customers reject assessments produced by its internal audit department even though the working papers are thorough and the findings candid.

profile.environment: 12,000 access reviews to verify · external auditors needing six weeks of access
profile.state: Audit window shorter than the population

stimuli.title: Exercising the plan before the day
stimuli.text: Marlow Regional Bank has a new incident response plan for payment fraud that has never been exercised, and the chief information security officer wants the team to find gaps in roles, contact paths and decision points at minimal cost and zero production risk. After two successful attempts at that, the team should actually perform its response actions against a realistic scenario while customer transactions stay unaffected. The bank must also prove its recovery site can process the transaction load, and a regulator wants the highest attainable assurance that processing genuinely fails over, with a maintenance window approved.

profile.organization: Marlow Regional Bank · continuity and response
profile.environment: Response plan never exercised · recovery site never carried live load · board has approved a window
profile.state: Four exercises being sequenced across the year

stimuli.title: One cycle and three places the data lives
stimuli.text: Wrenfield Analytics processes hospital claims for 40 payer clients. Its claims engine runs on a managed Kubernetes service in one cloud region, the seven-year archive sits in provider-encrypted object storage, and two reconciliation servers still run in a Columbus colocation cage Wrenfield owns outright. Wrenfield's testers hold a standing scanning permission from the cloud provider for their own tenant. The security committee has funded one assessment cycle. Its largest client's contract requires an independent audit of the environment holding that client's data, with a 30-day cure period for findings. The draft plan schedules a control self-assessment run by the platform owners and a vulnerability scan of the tenant, cites the provider's SOC 2 Type II for the platform, and puts the colocation cage out of scope.

profile.organization: Wrenfield Analytics · claims processing for hospital payers
profile.environment: one cloud region plus an owned colocation cage
profile.state: planning the annual assessment cycle

stimuli.title: What the metrics pack does not say
stimuli.text: Thistlewood Mutual, a 900-employee insurer in Des Moines, sends one security metrics pack to its risk committee each quarter. The current pack reports 100 percent completion of the annual awareness course, a 99.6 percent success rate across 480 nightly backup jobs, and no privileged accounts outstanding from the quarterly access review. A March tabletop then failed to restore the claims platform: the nightly job had been writing to a decommissioned share for eleven weeks and reported success every night. In the same quarter, an administrator account belonging to a leaver stayed enabled for 40 days, because the review sampled ten accounts out of 3,200. The committee has asked the CISO to redesign what is measured and who verifies it.

profile.regime: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law
profile.environment: on-premise data center with a hosted claims platform
profile.state: quarterly metrics under redesign

questions.question: Legal's draft reply threatens action under the terms of service. What should the security lead advise FIRST?

options.A: Ask the researcher to sign a non-disclosure agreement before the report is examined.
options.B: Establish a published reporting channel with safe-harbor terms, then reply through it.
options.C: Refer the report to the card brands so they can direct FinCorp's response to it.
options.D: Reproduce the finding and patch it before any reply is sent to the researcher.

questions.explanation: FinCorp has no route by which a report can arrive, so every reply it drafts is improvised, and improvised replies from Legal are how a ninety-day deadline becomes a press cycle. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-5(11) Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Public Disclosure Program is the precise and rarely quoted control: establish a public reporting channel for receiving reports of vulnerabilities in organizational systems and system components. NIST SP 800-218 RV.1.3 states the developer-side obligation, a policy addressing vulnerability disclosure and remediation with the roles and processes to support it. NIST SP 800-216 is the dedicated federal guideline on the subject. A is the right control for a different problem, since a non-disclosure agreement manages a paid engagement, not an unsolicited report from someone who owes FinCorp nothing. C is not the decision-maker's; FinCorp owns the system and the reply. D is a correct action but not the first one, because the clock runs whether or not anyone answers, and a silent patch invites publication. Build the channel, then use it.
questions.recallLine: A researcher reports a live flaw and Legal drafts a threat. What should the security lead advise first?

optionsShort.A: Ask for a non-disclosure agreement
optionsShort.B: Publish a channel with safe harbor
optionsShort.C: Refer it to the card brands
optionsShort.D: Reproduce and patch before replying

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: What governs confidentiality when FinCorp commissions a penetration test from a firm it pays?

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Who must be told once the scope of a cardholder-data exposure is established?

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: What does FinCorp owe its customers once a reported flaw has been confirmed?

NIST SP 800-218 | RV.1.3 vulnerability disclosure and remediation policy
NIST SP 800-216 named as the dedicated federal disclosure guideline

questions.question: The finding is reproduced. The VP of Engineering proposes shipping the fix in the release already scheduled for eleven weeks out. Which response BEST reflects how remediation should be decided?

options.A: Ship in the scheduled release, because unscheduled changes carry risks of their own.
options.B: Ship immediately, because any confirmed defect in a money path is an emergency.
options.C: Ask the researcher whether she will extend the ninety-day deadline to cover the release.
options.D: Rank it against the other open findings by exploitability and impact, then set the date.

questions.explanation: Remediation timing is a risk decision, and a risk decision needs a basis that survives being asked about later. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-5 Plan of Action and Milestones requires documented planned remediation actions to correct weaknesses noted during control assessments, with milestones, and RA-7 Risk Response requires the organization to respond to findings in accordance with its own risk tolerance. NIST SP 800-115 Chapter 8, Post-Testing Activities, covers turning findings into mitigation recommendations and a remediation plan. Ranking is what lets FinCorp defend either a rushed fix or a scheduled one. A is not the decision-maker's, treating schedule ownership as though it settled a risk question. B is a correct action but not the first one: urgency is very likely the right conclusion here, and it is still a conclusion rather than the method the question asks for. C is the right control for a different problem, because the researcher's clock is not FinCorp's risk basis. Decide by risk, then argue about the calendar.
questions.recallLine: When should a confirmed money-path defect be fixed, and on what basis is that decided?

optionsShort.A: Wait for the scheduled release
optionsShort.B: Ship immediately as an emergency
optionsShort.C: Ask for a deadline extension
optionsShort.D: Rank by exploitability and impact

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Who owns the release calendar, and what does that ownership actually decide?

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: What is the likely outcome once this finding has been ranked against the others?

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: What is worth discussing with a researcher when a fix genuinely cannot be delivered in ninety days?
